text:
Maya: Nightly eval threw a weird sampling regression on rdx-3b-q4 — sudden style/verbosity shift across ~30 prompts, lots more hallucinations. Can someone triage? :eyes:

Lee: Did we change sampling defaults in the rollout yesterday? I thought we pinned top_p/temp for evals.

Maya: Here's the diff from the eval job metadata: 
```
prev_run_config: {
  "temp": 0.2,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "top_k": 40,
  "seed": null
}
latest_run_config: {
  "temp": 0.2,
  "top_p": 0.9,
  "top_k": 40,
  "seed": 12345
}
```
Notice both top_p lowered and seed got set.

Sara: Where did the seed come from? eval infra shouldn't set a deterministic seed by default.

Lee: I think runtime changes added deterministic seeding for KV-cache warmups. There was a small PR. @rand-bot maybe logged seed at startup.

rand-bot: INFO: seed=12345 set by env REDWOOD_SEED=12345 at 2026-02-10T02:34:12Z

Maya: Example failure: prompt: "Summarize this legal clause in one sentence."
- expected concise: "Limits liability to X under Y."
- latest gen: long, repetitive paragraph with an invented case citation and extra hedging.

Sara: Lower top_p usually reduces tail noise, so I'd expect more conservative answers, not hallucinations. Strange.

Lee: Hypothesis: deterministic seed + caching + batching altered token-prob ties and sampling order; also config-merge bug may have set top_p=0.9 globally for the nightly pipeline.

Maya: Triage plan I ran: 
1) rerun nightly eval with seed=null & top_p=0.95 (override)
2) rerun with seed=12345 & top_p=0.95
3) compare quantized vs fp16 outputs

Lee: Running step 1 now: run id eval-1759000100 (ETA ~8m).

eval-bot: run eval-1759000100 started, config: temp=0.2 top_p=0.95 seed=null model=rdx-3b-q4

Lee: Results for run 1: pass rate jumped to ~92% (from 68% on the failing set). So reintroducing top_p=0.95 & seed=null fixes most cases.

Maya: Run 2 (seed=12345 & top_p=0.95) completed: pass rate ~75% — better than latest but still worse than seed=null. Seed seems to interact but isn't sole cause.

Sara: Could quantized softmax scaling / kernel changes alter logits slightly, so with a fixed seed you hit a different deterministic sample path that amplifies odd tokens?

Lee: Found relevant code: PR 479 changed float->quantized softmax scaling and PR 482 enabled deterministic seed at startup. Combined, rounding differences + deterministic sampling order explain changed outputs.

Maya: Action items: 
- rollback deterministic seeding in nightly eval infra until we understand interaction (Maya)
- open issue linking PR 479 & PR 482 for eng-runtime (Lee)
- add nightly eval variants that explicitly run seed=null and seeded runs and compare ngram/token-dist diffs (Sara)
- add gating check in eval CI: if sampling params (temp/top_p/top_k/seed) differ from baseline, emit alert and block auto-reporting

Lee: I'll open the issue and assign to @eng-runtime, add a small unit test comparing sampling distributions across seed variations.

Sara: Also update model onboarding checklist: when bringing up quantized models include sampling smoke tests with seed null and with a fixed seed to surface these interactions early.

Maya: Filed follow-ups: issue #2043 (Sampling drift triage) and PR #2050 (eval-compare param diff).

Lee: For now, re-run the failing subset on fp16 vs q4 with seed=null to confirm quantization isn't the only factor.

Maya: Thx all. If anyone sees more strange diffs, paste short before/after snippet here. :thumbsup:

rand-bot: NOTE: rolling back REDWOOD_SEED enforcement in nightly pipeline (temp change) — will revert env inject at 1759000200. :white_check_mark:

Sara: quick win: add a one-line note in onboarding docs about 'do not force seed during nightly evals' so PLs don't accidentally enable it.

Lee: PR for sampling distro unit test opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/2051 — CC @eng-runtime.

Maya: closing loop — re-ran full nightly with rollback, baseline pass rates restored. Leaving issue open for root cause analysis and adding more robust eval checks.

(End thread)
